text:
The night that mattered most for Valeri Nichushkin this fall was Nov. 3, when Columbus beat Colorado 7-2 and he scored against the team he won a Cup with in 2022. The Denver Post's Corey Masisak wrote ahead of it about why the Avalanche stuck with him through "multiple years of off-ice issues," quoting Nichushkin asking, "Is it going to be a good story, or bad story?" Two nights later he scored the shootout winner against Dallas.

On the ice the start is modest. He has 8 points in 15 games and only 19 shots, and his own chances are down to 0.49 expected goals per 60 from 1.07 last season. At 5v5 Columbus is about even with him on the ice.

In Colorado he was more than that. Evolving-Hockey had him helping on both ends last season, though with teammates in the 99th percentile. The question in Columbus is whether he can still get to the net without them. So far the shots say not yet.
headline: Nichushkin's new start is quieter than his last
